"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The default recipe gives only about 131k steps, which at 4,096 steps per update is about 32 PPO updates. That is very few, and it probably explains why seeds either take off (0.258) or get stuck (0.068). The budget formula rewards fewer epochs: 2 epochs gives about 243k steps and 1 epoch about 426k. Smaller rollouts also give more updates. A separate problem is that the +1 exact-build bonus comes at the end of a 10–20 step episode, and gamma 0.95 shrinks it a lot. That weakens the signal that rewards finishing exactly and ordering bricks correctly. Round 1 tests three separate levers: more updates with fewer epochs, many more samples at 1 epoch, and longer-horizon credit with less entropy. With seed noise near ±0.1, only large gains (mean ≥0.2) should count as real.
analyses.2: Five of the six seeds so far, across three different recipes, landed on exactly 0.0684 (35/512) on dev, and their train success is about the same. That looks like a fixed local optimum: probably a greedy fill strategy that only gets the easy designs exactly right. The one starting-architecture seed that escaped reached 0.258, so the bottleneck seems to be getting out of this trap, not the sample count. More updates, 3.25x the data and longer-horizon credit all failed to change it. Lowering entropy (r1c3) was slightly worse, which suggests keeping exploration higher. This round tests things that can help escape: much more entropy, smaller and more careful updates (lower learning rate, smaller clip) that avoid early collapse, and rollouts long enough to hold whole episodes so the +1 exact-build bonus reaches the gradient directly. Any of these that lifts a seed clearly above 0.07 counts as evidence.
analyses.3: Seeds land in one of two modes: a stuck mode at exactly 0.0684 (35 of 512 dev designs, probably a greedy-fill strategy that only gets the easy designs) and a good mode at about 0.26 to 0.33. Of the six recipe changes tried, only ent_coef 0.03 with everything else at the default reached the good mode, and only on one of its two seeds. These recipes all stayed stuck: more samples, fewer epochs, gentler updates, whole-episode rollouts, and a longer horizon with low entropy. Entropy 0.02 combined with other changes (r2c2, r2c3) also stayed stuck, so stronger exploration with the default update settings looks like the lever that matters. Escaping the stuck mode is mostly luck, so the goal is to raise the fraction of seeds that escape. This round pushes entropy to the cap, tries entropy 0.03 with a bit more data, and tries strong entropy with long-horizon credit, which was only tested before alongside low entropy.
analyses.4: Every low-entropy recipe (ent_coef 0.003 to 0.02) left both seeds at the stuck 0.068 mode, whatever the epochs, batch shape or learning rate. Raising ent_coef to 0.03 to 0.05 is the only change that got seeds out of it (0.20, 0.22, 0.29). The best result so far, r3c2, combined ent_coef 0.03 with 3 epochs (about 168k steps) and scored 0.29, but its two seeds were far apart (0.44 and 0.14), so seed noise is large. A long horizon (gamma 0.99, gae_lambda 0.95) hurt even with high entropy (0.084), which suggests a short horizon is better here. In this last round I refine the high-entropy, fewer-epochs region: more entropy with 3 epochs, a shorter horizon on the best recipe, and 2 epochs with high entropy. The 2-epoch runs that failed before used only ent_coef 0.02.
